issues.title: Independent component weights invalidate exact-solution cancellation

failure_location.quote: We estimate the residual as follows:

issues.failure_explanation: For u_ε=u and f_ε=f, the old bound based on the hatted approximation errors has a zero right-hand side. In contrast, eq:barRQ1 leaves the generally nonzero terms (φ_{θ¹}−1)∂_t u, −Σ_i(φ_{bar θ^i}−1)∂_{x_i x_i}u, (φ_{θ²}−1)v(u), and −(φ_{θ³}−1)f1_ω. Independently weighted endpoint data likewise do not cancel. The old proof omits all these terms, and arbitrary ρ need not make the negative neural penalty dominate them. The bilinear proofs repeat the same error with the additional (φ_{θ³}−1)fu term.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed vanishing-rate WeightedPINN existence bounds are not established for arbitrary independent bounded weights and arbitrary positive ρ. The special case in which all weights equal one is not affected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the independent weights but replace arbitrary positive ρ by a quantitative penalty-dominance condition. For each weight collection, let A be the total squared PDE and endpoint residual left by the weight deviations at the exact pair, including the additional fu term in the bilinear cases, and let B be the corresponding neural-weight penalty. Require ρB ≥ (1+η)A for some η>0, with a uniform version if a supremum over the weight class is claimed. Split each weighted residual into its approximation part and exact weight-mismatch part, absorb the latter and the cross terms into −ρB, and propagate this argument through all four existence theorems.
issues.why_classification: The omitted terms make the arbitrary-weight, arbitrary-ρ assertion genuinely false, so this is not a transcriptional or routine local defect. A complete repair needs new mismatch estimates and a substantive restriction relating ρ to the weights and exact solution data across four theorems. Nevertheless, the same independent-weight method, vanishing-loss form, and approximation architecture survive under that contained argument, so the loss and proof burden are moderate rather than serious.

issues.title: Space-time input dimension omitted from approximation exponents

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We first recall the definition of a feedforward neural network mapping $\mathbb{R}^d$ to $\mathbb{R}$ with width $\mathcal{W}$ and depth $\mathcal{L}$.

issues.failure_explanation: In the paper's notation d is the spatial dimension and also the generic neural-network input dimension. Since Q_T=Ω×(0,T) is a subset of R^{d+1}, the input-dimension parameter in the cited approximation result must be instantiated as d+1 for u_ε and f_ε. The old formulas in eq:udiff and eq:fdiff instead use denominators d, producing the unsupported faster rates −2/d, −4/d, and ultimately −1/d.
issues.overall_effect: All four existence theorems advertise a faster width-depth rate than the approximation step supports on the space-time domain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Instantiate the cited approximation theorem with input dimension D=d+1 on Q_T and q_T. Replace the intermediate exponents −2/d and −4/d by −2/(d+1) and −4/(d+1), adjust the width-depth versus mollification balance accordingly, and replace every final −1/d exponent by −1/(d+1) in the heat, wave, and two bilinear existence theorems.
issues.why_classification: Although d+1 is uniquely forced by the old source, the correction withdraws a coherent and substantively faster advertised width-depth rate, so it is neither a typo nor a same-guarantee minor repair. The recalculation is local and leaves recognizably comparable polynomial convergence results with unchanged proof architecture, making the issue moderate rather than serious.

issues.title: Nonlinear difference quotient drops an affine residual term
issues.failure_explanation: The preceding identity gives v(u_θ)−v(bar u)=V(u_θ−bar u), hence v(u_θ)=Vu_θ+v(bar u)−V bar u. The loss controls the residual containing v(u_θ), but the proof defines R with Vu_θ and omits v(bar u)−V bar u. That offset is generally nonzero, so the assumed loss does not control the R used in the energy estimate. The wave proof repeats the same substitution.
issues.overall_effect: The first state-stability estimate in each small-loss theorem is unsupported for a general globally Lipschitz nonlinearity. This is independent of the later control-identifiability and backward-heat defects.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the heat proof define R as the actual unweighted residual R=∂_t u_θ−Δu_θ+v(u_θ)−f_barθ 1_ω, and use the analogous definition with ∂_{tt} in the wave proof. Subtracting the equation for bar u then gives ∂_t hat u−Δhat u+Vhat u=R, or its wave analogue, exactly, so the assumed loss controls the forcing used in the energy estimate.
issues.why_classification: The proof makes a genuine algebraic substitution error, so the issue is more than a typo. However, replacing R by the already-defined nonlinear PINN residual is a short, routine correction that preserves the globally Lipschitz nonlinearity, every hypothesis, conclusion, norm, and rate in both affected proofs without a new lemma or construction.

issues.title: Terminal-data-only heat trajectory is not generally solvable

failure_location.quote: the above semilinear heat equation admits a unique solution. Consequently, \(\bar u\) is well defined.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let \(\bar u\in C\bigl([0,T];L^{2}(\Omega)\bigr)\cap L^{2}\bigl(0,T;H^{1}(\Omega)\bigr)\) be the weak solution of

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed problem for bar u prescribes bar u(T)=z₀ but no initial value. Forward heat well-posedness does not establish existence for this backward problem. For example, on Ω=(0,π), with v=0 and f_{bar θ}=0, take z₀(x)=Σ_{n≥1}n^{-2}sin(nx). It belongs to L², but any solution in C([0,T];L²) would have nth coefficient n^{-2}exp(n²(T−t)) at time t<T, which is not square summable. Hence the asserted bar u need not exist in the stated class, so all downstream estimates using it lack a valid input.
issues.overall_effect: The heat small-loss proof cannot start for general terminal data and neural controls; its energy and subsequent controllability arguments are consequently unestablished. The wave terminal construction is not affected by this parabolic obstruction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Abandon the terminal-only forward-heat construction. A valid replacement must assume or prove a quantitative near-reachability statement: after perturbing the neural control and initial datum by quantities of the loss scale, there is a forward weak trajectory ending at z_0. The comparison must then be redone with forward parabolic energy estimates and a justified null-controllability correction. Without such a new construction, the heat theorem must be restricted to an explicit backward-reachable compatibility class or withdrawn for general L2 terminal data.
issues.why_classification: Backward solvability fails for a natural, substantial part of the stated L2 terminal-data class, not merely for an exceptional degeneracy. Adding backward-reachability excludes the central advertised regime, while retaining general terminal data requires replacement of the core comparison and controllability architecture by a forward endpoint-correction argument. Thus every established complete route entails either major mathematical loss or essentially new proof architecture.

issues.title: Small loss does not identify a preselected exact control

diagnostic_evidence.quote: there exists a control $f \in L^2(q_T)$ such that the corresponding solution satisfies $u(T)=z_0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose definition of exact controllability supplies the existence of a control reaching the target, not uniqueness of that control. More decisively, take v=0 and zero initial and terminal data. For any nonzero smooth ψ compactly supported in (0,T)×ω, the heat pair u=ψ and f=∂_tψ−Δψ is admissible, as is the zero pair. The zero neural pair has supremal WeightedPINN loss zero, yet its distance to the nominated nonzero pair is positive, contradicting the claimed Cδ bound as δ tends to zero. Replacing ∂_t by ∂_{tt} gives the same wave counterexample. Thus the argument can at most select some nearby admissible pair, not the pair fixed in the statement.
issues.overall_effect: Both old stability theorems' fixed-pair state and control error conclusions are false without a uniqueness or selection principle. Only proximity to the set of admissible pairs can be inferred by the revised construction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the estimates relative to a nominated exact pair by estimates for the distance from (u_θ,f_barθ) to the set of admissible state-control pairs with the prescribed endpoints. In each proof, use the controllability result to choose a correction control having the asserted norm bound and define the comparison pair from that correction, rather than applying an existence estimate to the preselected difference f−f_barθ. Preserve the same state and control norms and the O(δ^{1/2}) distance rate in both heat and wave statements.
issues.why_classification: Zero loss cannot identify an arbitrarily preselected control when admissible controls are nonunique, so a substantive quantifier change is unavoidable. Nevertheless, proximity to the admissible set remains a recognizably comparable control-reconstruction guarantee with the same endpoint conditions, norms, and rate, and it follows through a contained but nontrivial controllability-based selection argument. This exceeds a minor repair but does not require major loss or global reconstruction for the nonuniqueness defect itself.
